name: batch-02
prompt:
Create ONE production game-icon SPRITE ATLAS, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows on a square canvas, ideally 2048x2048, genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha PNG. Input image is the user's approved style sheet, STYLE reference only. Match that soft tactile dimensional 3D collectible family: gentle warm upper-left diffuse studio light, rounded yet faithful forms, bright pastel/candy color, subtle ambient occlusion, restrained material detail. Each object's true material remains recognizable: paper, wood, glass, metal, woven cloth. No same-clay treatment on everything. No heavy dark outlines or flat vector art.

CRITICAL PACKAGING: There are EXACTLY NINE equal square virtual cells in a regular 3x3 grid. Draw ONE specified object/group centered within EACH virtual cell, at ONLY 48–52% of cell width/height, with at least 24% EMPTY TRANSPARENT MARGIN ON EVERY SIDE. Nothing may touch a virtual cell edge or cross into a neighbor. All strings, handles, leaves and shadows stay inside their own cell. Think SMALL MINIATURE ICONS with LARGE EMPTY GUTTERS, NOT large illustrations filling the sheet. Icon centers are x=16.67%,50%,83.33%, y=16.67%,50%,83.33% of the image. Each icon must fit in a box 18% of the overall image size. Empty space between shapes is essential. No visible grid lines, no backgrounds, no color squares, no borders, no captions, numbers, words, ID labels, titles or decorative props. Empty padding is genuine alpha transparency, NOT a drawn checkerboard. Top-left through bottom-right order is mandatory; do not swap cells. Each tile will be cropped at exact one-third boundaries into a separate icon. Keep centered and similarly weighted, readable at 32–66px. All objects fully in frame, no cropping. Only allow inscription glyphs explicitly specified in subject. Do not invent sacred symbols, cultural ornament, claims or text. No extra humans/hands/landscape/pedestals. Subject list in strict row-major order:
1. Cell row 1, column 1: A silver-colored scalloped lock pendant hangs from a warm orange-brown cotton cord loop, with three small silver drop ornaments below. Preserve the broad cloud-like curved outline and minimal linear face marks; no keyhole, key or invented inscription.
2. Cell row 1, column 2: A red lacquer-like barrel-headed mallet with golden end rings, a straight honey-brown wooden handle, round handle knob and short red cord tassel. Keep the broad horizontal drum-shaped head and simple unlettered surfaces.
3. Cell row 1, column 3: A small matte-painted turquoise house on a low ochre plinth, with a terracotta pitched roof, dark teal door and one cross-barred blue window edged in cream. Preserve the simple toy-sized house geometry and roof-tile lines, without added figures or lettering.
4. Cell row 2, column 1: A broad teal-rimmed platter with a cream interior holds orange and green vegetable strips and a salmon-pink fish slice; two pairs of brown wooden chopsticks reach inward from opposite upper corners. Preserve the lifted, loosely crossed food strips and shared central plate.
5. Cell row 2, column 2: A reclining gray-green stone ox with short horns, folded legs, broad muzzle and one visible dark eye rests on a pale rectangular stone base; a warm skin-toned hand reaches toward its forehead. Keep the ox as a still carved stone figure, without cloth, bells or gilded ornament.
6. Cell row 2, column 3: A warm skin-toned forearm and outstretched hand emerge from a teal sleeve; a thin ivory-white cotton cord wraps the wrist and forms a small tied loop with loose ends. Preserve the single cord and quiet horizontal hand pose, without bracelets or extra charms.
7. Cell row 3, column 1: A brown branching pussy-willow twig with three soft ivory catkins and small coral and yellow paper decorations stands beside a pink wrapped chocolate egg in a shallow tan woven basket. Keep the twig, catkins, paper accents and wrapped egg distinct.
8. Cell row 3, column 2: One irregular charcoal-black coal lump with a few blue-gray facets sits beside a small warm tan stone hearth with an amber flame and an open tan doorway. Preserve the single coal lump, low hearth and simple architectural framing, without extra gifts or figures.
9. Cell row 3, column 3: A prepared golden-brown sardine head with one dark eye is fixed to the top of a slender brown hiiragi twig, with paired sharp-edged dark green leaves below. Keep it as a fish head and Japanese hiiragi branch, without a whole fish, red berries or added decorations.
